title: The Best Thread Light Switches
subtitle: Every in-wall Thread switch we could find on Amazon, ranked.
intro: Thread light switches are still uncommon, so this list is short. We pulled the Thread switches and dimmers selling on Amazon and scored them on rating, review volume, and features. Every switch here needs a Thread border router.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

buyers_guide.q: What's a Thread border router and do I have one?
buyers_guide.a: It's the device that connects Thread gear to your home network. HomePod mini, HomePod (2nd gen), Apple TV 4K with Ethernet, Nest Hub (2nd gen), Nest Hub Max, and some Echo models have one built in. Home Assistant can also run one with a compatible radio.

buyers_guide.q: Why are there so few Thread switches?
buyers_guide.a: Most switch makers launched Matter over Wi-Fi first because it needs no extra hardware. Thread versions are arriving more slowly.

buyers_guide.q: Do I need a neutral wire?
buyers_guide.a: Most smart switches need one because the electronics stay powered when the light is off. Open the box and look for a bundle of white wires tied together at the back. If it's there, you have a neutral. Older homes, especially those built before the mid-1980s, often don't. If yours doesn't, pick a switch listed as no-neutral.

If you're comfortable replacing an ordinary switch, the job is similar: power off at the breaker, confirm it's dead with a tester, and match the wires. Check local code, and hire an electrician if the box is crowded, the wiring is aluminum, or you're not sure which wire is which.
